questions.questionText: Mitosis results in daughter cells that are:

options.text: Genetically identical to the parent cell
Genetically different from the parent cell

questions.explanation: Mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid daughter cells, used for growth and asexual reproduction.

questions.questionText: Which phase of the cell cycle includes DNA replication?
questions.explanation: The S (synthesis) phase is when DNA replication occurs, doubling the genetic material before division.

questions.questionText: During which phase do chromosomes line up at the equator of the cell?
questions.explanation: During metaphase, chromosomes are maximally condensed and align along the metaphase plate (cell equator) attached to spindle fibres.

questions.questionText: The cell cycle consists of:
questions.explanation: The cell cycle has two main stages: interphase (preparatory phases G1, S, G2) and the M phase (mitosis and cytokinesis).

questions.questionText: During anaphase, sister chromatids separate and move to:

options.text: The same side of the cell

questions.explanation: During anaphase, sister chromatids separate and are pulled by shortening spindle fibres to opposite poles of the cell.

questions.questionText: What is cytokinesis?
questions.explanation: Cytokinesis is the physical division of the cytoplasm, forming two separate daughter cells after mitosis.

questions.questionText: During prophase, chromosomes become visible because they:
questions.explanation: During prophase, chromatin condenses into visible chromosomes, the spindle forms, and the nuclear envelope breaks down.

questions.questionText: Centromeres hold:
questions.explanation: The centromere is the region where sister chromatids are held together and where spindle fibres attach during cell division.

questions.questionText: The G2 phase is important because:

options.text: The cell checks DNA and produces proteins for division

questions.explanation: G2 phase prepares the cell for mitosis by producing spindle proteins, checking for DNA errors, and ensuring replication is complete.

questions.questionText: In plant cells, cytokinesis occurs by:
questions.explanation: Plant cells form a cell plate (made of vesicles from Golgi) at the equator, which becomes the new cell wall between daughter cells.

questions.questionText: During telophase:

options.text: Nuclear envelopes reform and chromosomes uncoil

questions.explanation: During telophase, nuclear envelopes re-form around each set of chromosomes, chromosomes decondense, and the spindle breaks down.

questions.questionText: Spindle fibres are made of:
questions.explanation: Spindle fibres are microtubules made of tubulin protein that form the mitotic spindle to separate chromosomes.

questions.questionText: The G1 phase is characterised by:
questions.explanation: G1 is the first gap phase where the cell grows, synthesises proteins, and replicates organelles in preparation for DNA replication.

questions.questionText: Cancer is associated with:
questions.explanation: Cancer results from loss of cell cycle regulation, allowing cells to divide uncontrollably and form tumours.

questions.questionText: If a cell has 8 chromosomes at the start of interphase, how many chromosomes will each daughter cell have after mitosis?
questions.diagram: Chromosome number is preserved in mitosis.
questions.explanation: Mitosis preserves chromosome number. The 8 chromosomes duplicate to 16 chromatids (still 8 chromosomes) then divide to give 8 to each daughter cell.

questions.questionText: A checkpoint in the cell cycle ensures that:

options.text: Cells divide as quickly as possible
DNA is error-free and complete before division proceeds

questions.explanation: Cell cycle checkpoints (G1, G2, M) verify that conditions are suitable before proceeding, preventing propagation of damaged DNA.

questions.questionText: Why is mitosis important in wound healing?

options.text: It produces identical cells to replace damaged cells

questions.diagram: Mitosis replaces dead or damaged cells with identical copies, enabling tissue repair and wound healing.

questions.questionText: During which phase of mitosis does the nuclear envelope break down?
questions.explanation: The nuclear envelope breaks down during prophase, allowing spindle fibres to access and attach to chromosomes.

questions.questionText: Cyclins are:

options.text: Proteins that regulate the cell cycle

questions.explanation: Cyclins are regulatory proteins whose levels rise and fall during the cell cycle, activating CDKs to drive the cell through checkpoints.

questions.questionText: If a cell has a diploid number of 20 chromosomes (2n=20), after DNA replication in S phase the cell has:
questions.hint: After S phase but before division.
questions.explanation: After S phase, each chromosome has been replicated producing two sister chromatids. The chromosome count remains 20, but there are 40 chromatids.
